script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour. During the examination, you will hear several recordings. You will have time to read the instructions and the questions. You will also have time to check your work.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part A. Task 1. You are at the registration desk for the Food Tech Summit 2026. You will hear a conversation between a staff member and an exhibitor. Complete the registration form below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Good morning! Welcome to the Food Tech Summit 2026. We are expecting a huge crowd today—nearly three thousand attendees from across the globe. How can I help you with your registration today?

script.speaker: Justin
script.text: Hello! I'm here to pick up the badges and confirm the booth details for my team. My name is Justin Choi. I'm the CEO of Green Horizon Agri-Tech. Have you got us on your list?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Let me see... Green Horizon... Ah, yes, here it is. Green Horizon Agri-Tech. You're in the B-wing, right? Booth B14-C. That's in the 'Sustainable Innovation' zone, next to the hydroponic water-wall demonstration.

script.speaker: Justin
script.text: That's correct. Booth B14-C. And just checking the contact details—is my email correctly listed? It's choi.j@greenhorizon.hk.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Yes, Mr. Choi. I see choi.j@greenhorizon.hk. Everything seems in order. Now, regarding your equipment, our system shows you requested a heavy-duty rack. The weight is listed as 450 kilograms. Is that still accurate?

script.speaker: Justin
script.text: Yes, 450 kg. We have a lot of sensor arrays and LED panels. And the electrical load? I believe we requested 3000 Watts.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: 3000 Watts. Confirmed. I've flagged your booth for a high-voltage connection. Now, what sample content are you displaying?

script.speaker: Justin
script.text: We're showcasing our latest lab-grown protein strips. They're cultivated using our proprietary bioreactor technology.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Lab-grown protein strips. Fascinating. I see your FEHD Health Permit Ref is FEHD-8821-X. That checks out. Your booth set-up date is November 14, and teardown starts at 9:00 PM on the final day.

script.speaker: Justin
script.text: November 14 set-up, 9:00 PM teardown. Got it. And our insurance?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Your provider is Global Shield Underwriters. Everything is valid through the end of the month. You're all set, Mr. Choi. Enjoy the summit!

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. You will hear a keynote presentation by Dr. Beatrice Lam on 'The Vertical Revolution'. Listen to the presentation and complete the notes below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Dr Lam
script.text: Good morning, everyone. It's a pleasure to be here at the Food Tech Summit. My name is Dr. Beatrice Lam, and I'm the lead scientist at SkyFarms. Our facility is located in an old industrial block in Kwun Tong—a space that was previously a textile factory in the 1980s. By using 15,000 square meters of vertical growing surface across ten floors, we are producing more nutrient-dense food than 50 hectares of traditional farmland.

script.speaker: Dr Lam
script.text: Our system is a fully closed-loop hydroponic network, achieving a 98% water recycling efficiency. This is absolutely critical as freshwater becomes scarcer. But we don't just use solar energy; we've installed a proprietary system that captures CO2 directly from nearby traffic and pumps it into our grow-rooms. This increases our growth rate significantly. We achieve 22 full crop cycles a year.

script.speaker: Dr Lam
script.text: We currently produce 1.2 tons of leafy greens daily, distributed through our exclusive retail partner, Pure-Life Supermarkets. People often ask about costs. While nutrient solutions and labour are significant, the biggest operational cost is electricity for lighting. Our UV-C light sterilization system keeps pests away without chemicals.

script.speaker: Dr Lam
script.text: We offer public tours every second Saturday. Our initial funding came from the Agri-Tech Innovation Fund. The LED technology we use is branded 'Nutri-Glow', which mimics perfect summer sunlight every day. Thank you for your attention.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. You will hear a panel of three experts discussing the 'Lab-Meat Ethics'—the moral and practical implications of cultivated meat. Listen to the discussion and tick the correct boxes in the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome to our 'Future of Protein' panel. Joining us are Dr. Smith, Sarah Chen, and David Ho. Dr. Smith, is lab-grown meat ready for the masses?

script.speaker: Dr Smith
script.text: Scientifically, we're close. We can grow cells in 10,000-liter tanks. But production scalability is the massive wall we're hitting. Thermal management at that scale is incredibly complex.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I focus on the ethical side. For me, the primary win is animal welfare ethics. No slaughter, no feedlots, and 90% less land use. We've moved to synthetic amino acids as a growth medium, so no animal-derived serum is needed.

script.speaker: David
script.text: From a consumer standpoint, my priority is price parity with traditional meat. Currently, lab-meat costs about 450 dollars per kilogram. Until we hit parity, mainstream adoption will remain low.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: What about regulation?

script.speaker: Dr Smith
script.text: The Food Safety Center is our FDA-equivalent local department. All products need the 'Cultivated' labeling prefix. We're holding a public tasting at the Science Park Bistro next month.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Startups can email protein-tech@epd.gov.hk for inquiries. The projected market share by 2040 is 35%.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. You will hear three stakeholders discussing the '2050 Food Strategy' for Hong Kong. Listen to their conversation and complete the matrix below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Today we're joined by a Farmer, a Tech CEO, and a Nutritionist to discuss the 2050 Food Strategy. Farmer, what's your view on imports?

script.speaker: Farmer
script.text: We import over 90% of our food. Local farms need stronger protection from cheap overseas produce. Direct cash grants are better than tax breaks because small farmers can't wait for end-of-year rebates. I recommend setting up a Farmers' Cooperative Board.

script.speaker: Tech CEO
script.text: I disagree. Vertical farming can replace 30% of vegetable imports within a decade. But subsidies should fund R&D, not operations. I propose launching a Public-Private Agri-Tech Lab.

script.speaker: Nutritionist
script.text: Both views have merit. But diversified sourcing is still essential for food security. Subsidies must include nutrition education programs. I recommend mandating 'Farm-to-School' lunch programs so children understand where food comes from.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Can we find consensus?

script.speaker: Tech CEO
script.text: Let's agree on pilot programs by Q2 2027.

script.speaker: Farmer
script.text: Agreed, as long as youth employment in agri-tech is a key priority.

script.speaker: Nutritionist
script.text: And the next step should be to submit a unified proposal to the Legislative Council.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of Part A. You now have five minutes to study the Part B Question-Answer Book and the Data File. (300-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Integrated Skills Recording. You will now hear a briefing from the CEO of Urban Nutrients, Janice Wong, to the Project Manager regarding the upcoming tasks. Listen carefully and take notes as you will need this information to complete the tasks in Part B.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Good morning. I'm glad we're finally getting started on these tasks. We have a lot to do before the Q4 rollout. When you write that letter to the Traditional Farmers' Union for Task 8, please don't just repeat the brochure points. Emphasize that we aren't just creating tech jobs for specialists. Mention that we are specifically looking to hire people with 'soil expertise' and 'community farming experience' to bridge the gap between high-tech and traditional agriculture. That's a key detail not in the Data File yet.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Moving on to the internal memo for Task 9—don't just list the budget gap. Propose a specific 'Harvest Festival Week' in September to fix the publicity issue. We need to get local food bloggers involved to build trust. And for the public social media post in Task 10, make sure to use a friendly, non-corporate tone. Use the phrase 'Green Plate Revolution' and make it sound like a neighbour talking to a neighbour.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: One last thing—I just heard from the Food Safety Center. They insist that we describe our lab-meat screening process as 'Pharmaceutical Grade'. That's the specific term they want us to use in our responses to citizens like Mr. David Chan. 'Pharmaceutical Grade'. Got it? Good. I expect those drafts on my desk by the end of the day. Good luck.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of the Integrated Skills recording. You now have 1 hour and 10 minutes to complete your tasks. Stop writing when you hear the signal at the end of the examination.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (4200-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Stop writing now. The examination is over. Please stay in your seats until your scripts have been collected.

data_file.title: Minutes of the 3rd Food Security Steering Committee Meeting
data_file.content:
Date: March 15, 2026
Location: Conference Room B, Gov HQ

Attendees: Mr. K.W. Ho (Food Bureau), Ms. Sarah Jenkins (Public Relations), Dr. Simon Lee (Nutrition Consultant).

Main Points:
1. Mr. Ho noted that public trust in lab-grown meat is currently low (approx 28% approval). We need to address farmers' fear of 'market displacement'.
2. Ms. Jenkins suggested a 'Green Plate Revolution' campaign. The goal is to highlight how agri-tech creates new categories of jobs (e.g., Vertical Farm Technicians, Cultured Meat Inspectors).
3. Action Item: Draft a persuasive letter to the Farmers' Union to calm nerves before the Q4 2026 rollout.
4. Note: Avoid technical jargon. Use the 'Harvest for All' slogan.

data_file.title: Food Tech Summit 2026: Official Program Highlights
data_file.content:
A Vision for the Future:
- Total Investment: $1.2 Billion HKD.
- Key Pillar: Vertical Farming (15,000 sq m already active in Kwun Tong).
- Upcoming: Food Safety Center guidelines to be published by October.

Why Agri-Tech?
Sustainability is not just about yield; it's about reducing import dependency. Our vertical farms have already cut transport emissions by 40% in the pilot district.

data_file.title: Email from a Concerned Citizen (Mr. David Chan)
data_file.content:
To: Food Bureau Feedback
Subject: Health Concerns regarding Lab-Grown Meat

I live in Sha Tin and I am extremely uncomfortable with the idea of feeding my children 'cultivated' protein. Who is monitoring the synthetic amino acids? Is the process safe? I heard rumours that Green Horizon is cutting corners on safety. Please clarify immediately or I will organise a local boycott.

data_file.title: Editorial: The Import Dependency and the $3,000 Question
data_file.content:
South China Morning Post - March 20, 2026

While the government brags about 'Food Tech' status, thousands of traditional farmers are being left behind. Dr. Lam's proposal for a $3,000 subsidy is a good start, but it won't fix the lack of land access which is a barrier for many. We need a 'Food Safety Net' that includes both technology and lifelong training for rural workers.

data_file.title: Urgent Note from CEO Janice Wong (Post-it Note)
data_file.content:
To: Project Manager

Just saw David Chan's email (Doc 3). We MUST reply to him. Be firm but polite. Explain that data is ANONYMIZED and never sold. Also, mention the Food Safety Center is overseeing this. We can't afford a boycott right now. Also, for the internal memo (Task 9), make sure you mention we are hiring 150 'Farm Tech Trainers' to show we are creating jobs!

data_file.title: Table 1: Food Tech Budget vs. Actual Spending (Q1 2026)
data_file.content:
Category | Budgeted | Actual | Status
--------------------------------------------
Hardware | $300M | $330M | Over-budget
Consultancy | $100M | $90M | Under-budget
Publicity | $80M | $30M | Critical Gap
Staffing | $200M | $190M | On track

Note: The 'Publicity' gap is why the public is currently so skeptical. We need to increase social media presence immediately.

data_file.title: Viral Post from 'HK Farmers Union'
data_file.content:
Shared 3,800 times:
'THEY ARE REPLACING US! The new Food Tech policy is a death sentence for the farming sector. They talk about "innovation" but we know it means "redundancy." Stand with us on April 15th! #NoToLabMeat #ProtectOurFarmers'

data_file.title: Internal Memo: Staffing Update
data_file.content:
Internal Use Only
Subject: New Role Creation - Farm Tech Trainers

To counter the negative PR, we are announcing the creation of 150 'Farm Tech Trainer' roles. These staff will be deployed to rural centres to teach 'Digital Farming Literacy'. This proves our Food Tech policy creates jobs for humans too!

data_file.title: Tech News Daily: Pure-Life Supermarkets Partnership
data_file.content: Pure-Life Supermarkets has officially signed a deal to stock vertical-farm produce in all 45 Hong Kong outlets. This move aims to reduce import dependency and guarantee 48-hour freshness for leafy greens.

data_file.title: Draft Section: Cultivated Meat Labelling
data_file.content: Clause 3.1: All cultivated meat products must carry the prefix 'Cultivated' in both English and Chinese. Nutritional data must be verified by the Food Safety Center before market release. No cross-border sale of unverified produce is permitted.
